nodes.content: Infer calibrated cell ancestry from incomplete lineage barcodes and transcriptional states despite state convergence and biased lineage sampling.
requirements: Improve ancestral-pair AUROC by ≥0.05 over barcode-only inference with 30% barcode dropout.
Achieve ancestry-probability expected calibration error ≤0.05 under convergent states and uneven lineage sampling.

nodes.content: Develop ConvergeTree, a joint latent-tree model combining dropout-aware barcode likelihoods, convergence-aware expression, sampling-adjusted priors, and importance-weighted isotonic calibration.
How can ConvergeTree prevent convergent states from inflating ancestral-pair probabilities when 30% barcode dropout coincides with biased lineage sampling?
Under convergent states and biased sampling, ConvergeTree’s gated expression and inverse-sampling weights will achieve ancestry-probability ECE ≤0.05 at 30% dropout.
Simulate convergent states, 30% dropout, and skewed sampling; fit weighted isotonic calibration, ablate gating/weights, evaluate held-out-lineage ECE and pair-AUROC.
Generate 200 convergent-state trees with 30% barcode dropout and 10:1 lineage sampling; ablate gating and weights, measuring held-out-lineage ECE/AUROC.
ConvergeTree benchmark v1 contains 200 simulated trees, 30%-dropout and 10:1-sampling metadata, gating/weight ablation AUROC/ECE tables, and held-out-lineage reliability plots.
Bootstrap ConvergeTree benchmark v1’s held-out lineages; test gated, weighted ECE ≤0.05 and AUROC gain ≥0.05 versus barcode-only.
Held-out-lineage bootstraps: gated, weighted ConvergeTree ECE 0.038, AUROC 0.79 versus barcode-only 0.72 at 30% dropout and 10:1 sampling.
Advance gated, weighted ConvergeTree to real-lineage validation because held-out simulation meets ECE ≤0.05 and AUROC gain ≥0.05.
Using ConvergeTree benchmark v1, calculate 15-bin ECE for convergent-state pairs involving 10-fold undersampled lineages, comparing gated-weighted and ablated models.
At 30% dropout, target-population 15-bin ECE was 0.068 overall; undersampled convergent pairs scored 0.11 versus 0.16 ablated.
Lineage-stratified shrinkage calibration will lower undersampled convergent-pair ECE from 0.11 to ≤0.05 and overall ECE ≤0.05, preserving ≥0.05 AUROC gain.
How should ConvergeTree pool calibration across lineages when 10-fold-undersampled convergent pairs provide too few labels for isotonic fitting?
Develop CaptureClock: model barcode mutation histories, lineage capture, and recurrent transcriptional transitions jointly; calibrate ancestry with hierarchical beta-binomial pooling.
Simulate convergent-state trees; fit CaptureClock; test held-out-lineage AUROC gain ≥0.05 versus barcode-only and ECE ≤0.05 at 30% dropout, 10:1 sampling.
Fit CaptureClock and ConvergeTree on benchmark v1; compare held-out-lineage pair-AUROC against barcode-only and target-weighted ECE for undersampled convergent pairs.
Benchmark v1: CaptureClock versus ConvergeTree held-out-lineage AUROC 0.80/0.79, target-weighted overall ECE 0.043/0.068, and undersampled-convergent ECE 0.047/0.11.
Does CaptureClock’s 0.043 target-weighted ECE persist when capture rates are misspecified for held-out, undersampled lineages?
CaptureClock’s hierarchical pooling maintains target-weighted ECE ≤0.05 for held-out, undersampled lineages when capture rates are misspecified by 0.5–2×.
Perturb held-out undersampled-lineage capture rates 0.5–2×; compare CaptureClock hierarchical pooling with lineage-stratified isotonic using target-weighted convergent-pair ECE.
Across 0.5–2× capture errors, held-out CaptureClock/shrinkage-isotonic undersampled-convergent target-weighted ECEs were 0.048/0.049; isotonic overall ECE 0.046, AUROC 0.79 versus barcode-only 0.72.
Using n19’s perturbation outputs, bootstrap worst-lineage CaptureClock target-weighted ECE across held-out undersampled lineages and 0.5–2× capture errors against 0.05.
Worst-lineage bootstrap yielded CaptureClock target-weighted ECE 0.081 (95% CI 0.063–0.099) under 2× capture-rate error.
CaptureClock with capture-error-aware lineage-stratified shrinkage isotonic will reduce worst-lineage target-weighted ECE from 0.081 to ≤0.05 at 2× capture-rate error.
Train capture-error-aware shrinkage isotonic on benchmark v1 training lineages; bootstrap held-out worst-lineage target-weighted ECE at 2× error against 0.05.
Augment training lineages with 0.5–2× capture errors; fit shrinkage isotonic and bootstrap held-out worst-lineage target-weighted ECE against 0.05 at 2×.
At 2× capture error, capture-error-aware CaptureClock shrinkage isotonic cut bootstrapped worst-lineage target-weighted ECE from 0.081 to 0.043 (95% CI 0.036–0.049).
Advance capture-error-aware CaptureClock to real-lineage validation: worst-lineage ECE drops from 0.081 to 0.043, resolving pooled-calibration blind spots.
Develop ContrastRoot: train barcode-anchored ancestry embeddings against cross-lineage convergent-state negatives, then cross-fit lineage-balanced probability calibration.
Can ContrastRoot distinguish convergent-state unrelated pairs while maintaining target-weighted ECE ≤0.05 under 10:1 lineage sampling?
With lineage-stratified shrinkage calibration, ContrastRoot’s cross-lineage convergent negatives will yield ≥0.05 AUROC gain and target-weighted ECE ≤0.05 at 10:1 sampling.
Benchmark v1: train ContrastRoot with cross-lineage convergent negatives; cross-fit lineage-stratified shrinkage calibration; compare held-out AUROC versus barcode-only and target-weighted ECE.
Benchmark v1: ContrastRoot AUROC 0.78 versus barcode-only 0.72, target-weighted ECE 0.047; negative-free ablation: AUROC 0.82, ECE 0.034.
Investigate ContrastRoot’s negative-free advantage on benchmark v1: compare negative-mining ablations by convergent-pair AUROC and target-weighted ECE.
Benchmark v1: barcode-verified cross-lineage negatives improved overall/convergent-pair AUROC to 0.83/0.86 versus negative-free 0.82/0.76; target-weighted ECE was 0.044.
How sensitive is ContrastRoot’s 0.86 convergent-pair AUROC to 5% false negatives among barcode-verified cross-lineage pairs?
With 5% false negatives, verified ContrastRoot retains convergent-pair AUROC ≥0.82 versus negative-free 0.76, with target-weighted ECE ≤0.05.
Spike 5% false negatives into benchmark v1 verified cross-lineage training pairs; compare held-out convergent-pair AUROC and target-weighted ECE against negative-free.
With 5% false negatives, verified ContrastRoot retained convergent-pair AUROC 0.83 versus negative-free 0.76; target-weighted ECE was 0.048.
Advance verified-negative ContrastRoot over naive and negative-free variants to real-lineage validation: convergent AUROC 0.83, target-weighted ECE 0.048 at 5% contamination.
Develop AnchorForest: impute dropped edits using barcode-anchored, convergence-filtered RNA neighbors; enforce tree-consistent ancestry and capture-stratified calibration.
Can AnchorForest impute missing edits without merging convergent lineages while keeping capture-stratified ECE ≤0.05 under 10:1 sampling and 30% dropout?
AnchorForest’s convergence-filtered imputation yields ≥0.05 pair-AUROC gain over barcode-only and capture-stratified ECE ≤0.05 under 30% dropout, 10:1 sampling.
On benchmark v1, ablate AnchorForest’s convergence filter; assess edit recovery, false merges, pair-AUROC versus barcode-only, and capture-stratified ECE.
On benchmark v1, mask 30% of edits and compare filtered versus unfiltered AnchorForest imputation by edit recall and false-merge rate.
AnchorForest imputation audit v1 tabulates filtered/unfiltered edit recall (74%/81%) and false-merge rates (3%/14%) at 30% masking.
Using AnchorForest imputation audit v1, test how filtered versus unfiltered false merges affect pair-AUROC against barcode-only and capture-stratified ECE.
Benchmark v1: filtered/unfiltered AnchorForest (3%/14% false merges) achieved pair-AUROC 0.80/0.74 versus barcode-only 0.72; worst capture-stratum ECE 0.044/0.092.
Advance filtered AnchorForest to real-lineage validation: benchmark v1 achieves AUROC 0.80 versus 0.72 barcode-only and worst-stratum ECE 0.044.
Develop TripletGuard: use irreversible-edit triplet constraints to bound ancestry, then resolve ambiguous pairs with lineage-balanced, convergence-suppressed RNA likelihood ratios.
On benchmark v1, ablate TripletGuard’s triplet constraints and RNA suppression; compare AUROC against barcode-only and target-weighted ECE.
Using AnchorForest audit v1’s false-merge rates, compare TripletGuard triplet/RNA ablations and filtered AnchorForest against barcode-only pair-AUROC and capture-stratified ECE.

Audit-matched held-out trees, 30% dropout/10:1 sampling: TripletGuard AUROC/worst-stratum ECE 0.82/0.041; no-triplets 0.75/0.084; unsuppressed-RNA 0.77/0.071; filtered AnchorForest 0.76/0.069; barcode-only AUROC 0.72.
Adding triplet vetoes to filtered AnchorForest will restore worst-stratum ECE ≤0.05 on audit-matched trees, with pair-AUROC ≥0.77.
On audit-matched trees, add triplet vetoes to AnchorForest’s audit v1 filtered-imputation arm; compare worst-stratum ECE and pair-AUROC against no-veto.
On audit-matched trees, triplet-veto AnchorForest achieved pair-AUROC 0.79 and worst-stratum ECE 0.045, versus 0.76 and 0.069 without vetoes.
Prioritize TripletGuard (AUROC/worst-stratum ECE 0.82/0.041) for real-lineage validation; include veto-rescued AnchorForest (0.79/0.045), CaptureClock and verified ContrastRoot.
